_comment: Know Your India quiz bank. Option index 'answer' is the correct one; options are shuffled at play time.

questions.q: What is the capital city of India?
questions.fact: New Delhi has served as India's capital since 1911.

questions.q: Which is India's longest river?
questions.fact: The Ganga flows about 2,525 km from the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.q: Which is India's highest mountain peak?
questions.fact: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) sits on the India-Nepal border; K2 lies in Pakistan-administered territory.

questions.q: How many states does India have?
questions.fact: India has 28 states and 8 union territories.

questions.q: Which is India's largest state by area?
questions.fact: Rajasthan covers more than 342,000 square kilometres.

questions.q: Which state is called 'God's Own Country'?
questions.fact: Kerala is famous for its backwaters, beaches and greenery.

questions.q: The Taj Mahal stands in which city?
questions.fact: It was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.q: What is India's national animal?
questions.fact: The Bengal tiger was named India's national animal in 1973.

questions.q: What is India's national bird?
questions.fact: The peacock was declared the national bird in 1963.

questions.q: What is India's national flower?
questions.fact: The lotus is admired for blooming clean even from muddy water.

questions.q: What is India's national fruit?
questions.fact: India grows hundreds of mango varieties, including Alphonso and Dasheri.

questions.q: What is India's national tree?
questions.fact: The banyan can grow huge aerial roots that look like extra trunks.

questions.q: What is the currency of India?
questions.fact: The rupee symbol ₹ was officially adopted in 2010.

questions.q: Which festival is known as the 'Festival of Lights'?
questions.fact: Diwali is marked by lighting rows of small clay lamps called diyas.

questions.q: Which festival is known as the 'Festival of Colours'?
questions.fact: People throw coloured powder called gulal to celebrate the arrival of spring.

questions.q: India's men's hockey team has won how many Olympic gold medals?
questions.fact: India dominated Olympic hockey for decades, winning golds from 1928 to 1980.

questions.q: Who is known as the 'Father of the Nation' in India?
questions.fact: Gandhi led India's independence movement through non-violent protest.

questions.q: Who was India's first Prime Minister?
questions.fact: Nehru served as Prime Minister from 1947 until his death in 1964.

questions.q: Who was India's first President?
questions.fact: Rajendra Prasad held office from 1950 to 1962.

questions.q: In which year did India gain independence from British rule?
questions.fact: India became independent on 15 August 1947.

questions.q: In which year did India become a republic?
questions.fact: India adopted its Constitution and became a republic on 26 January 1950.

questions.q: Who wrote India's national anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.fact: Tagore, a Bengali poet, also won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913.

questions.q: Who wrote 'Vande Mataram', India's national song?
questions.fact: It first appeared in his 1882 novel Anandamath.

questions.q: How many colours are on the Indian flag?
questions.fact: The flag has saffron, white and green bands with a navy blue wheel.

questions.q: What symbol sits at the centre of the Indian flag?
questions.fact: The wheel is taken from an Ashoka pillar at Sarnath.

questions.q: How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra have?
questions.fact: The 24 spokes are said to represent the hours of the day.

questions.q: Which river is considered the holiest in Hinduism?
questions.fact: Millions bathe in the Ganga each year, especially during the Kumbh Mela.

questions.q: The Thar Desert lies mainly in which state?
questions.fact: It is one of the most densely populated deserts in the world.

questions.q: Which mountain range runs along India's northern border?
questions.fact: The Himalayas contain many of the world's highest peaks.

questions.q: Which is India's smallest state by area?
questions.fact: Goa covers under 3,702 square kilometres.

questions.q: Which union territory was once a French colony?
questions.fact: France returned Puducherry to India in 1954.

questions.q: Which city is nicknamed the 'Silicon Valley of India'?
questions.fact: Bengaluru is home to thousands of technology companies.

questions.q: Which city is known as the 'City of Joy'?
questions.fact: Kolkata is famous for its trams, literature and sweets.

questions.q: Which city is called the 'Pink City'?
questions.fact: Jaipur's old city was painted pink in 1876 to welcome a royal visitor.

questions.q: Which city is called the 'Blue City'?
questions.fact: Many houses in old Jodhpur are painted a striking blue.

questions.q: Which city is nicknamed the 'City of Lakes'?
questions.fact: Udaipur is built around several artificial and natural lakes.

questions.q: Assam is especially famous for producing which crop?
questions.fact: Assam grows a large share of the world's tea.

questions.q: Which Indian epic tells the story of Rama and Sita?
questions.fact: It was composed by the sage Valmiki.

questions.q: Which epic contains the Bhagavad Gita?
questions.fact: The Gita is Krishna's conversation with the warrior Arjuna.

questions.q: Which classical dance form comes from Tamil Nadu?
questions.fact: It is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India.

questions.q: Which classical dance form from Kerala uses elaborate face paint?
questions.fact: Performers can take hours to apply their vivid make-up.

questions.q: Which classical dance form from North India is known for fast spins?
questions.fact: Kathak developed in the courts of North Indian kings.

questions.q: Sitar and tabla are both types of what?
questions.fact: The sitar is a stringed instrument and the tabla a pair of hand drums.

questions.q: Which Indian scientist won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930?
questions.fact: He discovered how light changes when it passes through matter — the Raman effect.

questions.q: Who is known as the 'Missile Man of India' and later became President?
questions.fact: Kalam helped develop India's satellite and missile programmes.

questions.q: What is India's space agency called?
questions.fact: ISRO stands for the Indian Space Research Organisation.

questions.q: What was India's 2023 mission that landed near the Moon's south pole?
questions.fact: India became the first country to land near the lunar south pole.

questions.q: What was India's first mission to Mars called?
questions.fact: It reached Mars orbit in 2014 on its very first attempt.

questions.q: How many times has India won the men's Cricket World Cup?
questions.fact: India lifted the trophy in 1983 and 2011.

questions.q: Who captained India to their first Cricket World Cup win in 1983?
questions.fact: India beat the West Indies in the final at Lord's.

questions.q: Which cricketer is nicknamed the 'Master Blaster'?
questions.fact: Tendulkar scored 100 international centuries during his career.

questions.q: Which Indian city hosts the annual Pushkar Camel Fair?
questions.fact: Thousands of camels, traders and tourists gather there each year.

questions.q: Which festival involves flying kites to mark the start of the harvest season?
questions.fact: Gujarat holds an especially famous International Kite Festival.

questions.q: Onam, the harvest festival with snake-boat races, is celebrated in which state?
questions.fact: Onam also features the flower carpet design called pookalam.

questions.q: Pongal, a major harvest festival, is celebrated mainly in which state?
questions.fact: Families cook the festival dish, also called pongal, in a new clay pot.

questions.q: Bihu is a major festival of which state?
questions.fact: Bihu is celebrated with traditional dance and music three times a year.

questions.q: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in which state?
questions.fact: It brings together many of Nagaland's tribal communities each December.

questions.q: The Sundarbans mangrove forest, home to the Royal Bengal Tiger, is found in which state?
questions.fact: It is the world's largest mangrove forest, shared with Bangladesh.

questions.q: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is in which state?
questions.fact: Kaziranga is home to the largest population of the species in the world.

questions.q: The Great Rann of Kutch, a vast white salt marsh, is found in which state?
questions.fact: It hosts a colourful cultural festival called the Rann Utsav.
